title: A city of projects
say: Each building is one project I built with Claude Code. Taller means more work. The roof colour says what it needs from me.
repo: Every building is a real folder on disk. The app only reads three things in it: the git history, Claude's chat logs, and one small note file. It never changes anything.
do: Point at the legend in the bottom right. Click its title to shrink it.

title: It started with one note
say: When a Claude session ends, it writes a short note: what I was doing, what to do next, and how I know it works. Weeks later I'd read it and wonder: is this still true? This app answers that.
repo: The note is `calculator/.claude/session-state.md`. NEXT ACTION and PROOF on screen are copied straight from it.
do: Click Open in VS Code and show the note file itself. Then come back.

title: What good looks like
say: PASS. The proof is not just a claim. The tests really ran, and the commit it names really exists.
repo: The note says `Ran 6 tests, OK; commit ...`. The app asked git about that commit, and git found it.

title: Break it live
say: Now I'll change the code but not the note. Watch this building.
repo: The command below adds a line to `calculator/README.md` and commits it. The note stays the same, so the note is now older than the code.
do: Second terminal, in the repo folder: py demo/make_demo.py --commit calculator . Wait 10 seconds, press F5.

title: It noticed
say: STALE. The roof is dashed and the check fails. The note was written before the newest work, so the app stops trusting it.
repo: Newest commit: `Live change during the demo`, a few seconds old. The note is older than that. The app compares the two times.
do: Now: py demo/make_demo.py --checkpoint calculator , press F5. It passes again.

title: Fixed by a fresh note
say: Writing a new note fixed it. That's what a Claude session does at the end, with the /coc-checkpoint skill.
repo: `--checkpoint` rewrote `calculator/.claude/session-state.md`. Its PROOF now names the new commit, so git can check it again.
do: Point at the PROOF line: the commit in it is the one you just made.

title: Stale on its own
say: Nobody touched this one on stage. Someone committed after the note was written, so the next step might already be done.
repo: The note in `habit-tracker` was written hours before its newest commit, `Streak keeps yesterday when today is unchecked`.

title: A commit that doesn't exist
say: The note says: shipped, tests pass, commit 4f9e2a1. The app asked git. That commit was never made. No AI needed to catch it.
repo: `pomodoro-timer/.claude/session-state.md` names commit `4f9e2a1`. `git log` in that folder has no such commit.

title: A quote that doesn't match
say: The note quotes a file: 'two hours a day'. The file really says 'two hours a week'. Quotes are checked word for word.
repo: `invoice-parser/NOTES.md` says `about two hours a week`. The note quotes it as `about two hours a day`.
do: Point at WHY and the gate question.

title: 'Continue' is not a next step
say: When a check fails, the app asks the one question to fix first. Here the next step just says 'continue', and one blocker has no owner.
repo: `url-shortener/.claude/session-state.md` has next_action `continue`, and the blocker `rate limiting is still undecided` names nobody.

title: Waiting on me
say: A blocker with my name on it shows up as 'waiting on you' at the top. That's my to-do list every morning.
repo: The note in `chatbot-frontend` has the blocker `Me [M]: pick the model provider`. `[M]` means it's mine.
do: Point at the clay '2 waiting on you' button at the top.

title: The story, told by Claude
say: How it started, where it is now, and every session as a chapter. Claude named each chapter. Nobody typed this by hand.
repo: Read from Claude's chat logs for this folder: the first prompt, the latest prompt, and the title Claude gave each session.
do: Scroll to HOW IT STARTED and the chapter list.

title: Checked, or only written down
say: All projects, failing ones first. For each one: what the app checked, yes or no, and what is only someone's word.
repo: Nothing new is read here. The same note files and git history, put side by side in one list.
do: Point at the checks count at the top, then scroll to pomodoro-timer and invoice-parser: each has one 'no'.

title: Take it home
say: End every session with three things: the next step, proof it works, and who owns each blocker. Then check the note against the code before you trust it.
repo: Want to look yourself? Every project here opens in VS Code. `demo.code-workspace` in the demo folder opens all of them at once.
do: Press T to hide this guide for questions.
